answers.explanation: A subnet is public because its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to an Internet Gateway — map-public-ip alone is not enough. Night 9 lab step: attach IGW + public route.
NAT must reach the internet through an IGW route on its (public) subnet's route table. Night 9 lab places NAT in public-a.
Single-NAT-in-one-AZ is a cost tradeoff — AZ-a outage kills outbound NAT for all private subnets. Exam: NAT per AZ for HA vs cost (d4-t4-cp-1).
NAT Gateway requires an Elastic IP allocation in VPC scope. Night 9 lab: allocate-address before create-nat-gateway.
DNS resolves names but private subnets still need NAT or endpoints for traffic to reach AWS APIs. Night 9: modify-vpc-attribute DNS flags.
Fargate in private subnets needs outbound path (NAT or ecr.api + ecr.dkr + S3 endpoints) plus execution role ECR permissions — not inbound SG rules. Night 10 prep.
Subnet behavior is defined by route table association, not naming. Associate with the private RT (NAT route). Night 9 lab associate_rt calls.
S3 gateway endpoints are free and route S3 prefix lists off NAT. week2-vpc-plan.md / Night 8 Q6.
DISABLED = no public IP on the task ENI; private subnet egress via NAT or endpoints. Exam: awsvpc assignPublicIp behavior.
RunTask awsvpc config needs subnets[] and securityGroups[] — private subnets + task SG. Exam networking for Fargate.
